instruction: Create a Markdown file named "README.md" through VS Code and save it to the Desktop directory at "/home/user/Desktop".

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a Markdown file on Desktop using VS Code. Evaluator checks for 'README.md' in /home/user/Desktop. Same difficulty as original - just different file type.

llm_judge_reasons: WRONG METRIC FUNCTION: Uses 'is_extension_installed' (designed for VS Code extension checking) instead of proper file verification metric like 'compare_answer'

INCOMPLETE VERIFICATION: Only checks if 'README.md' appears in ls output, does not verify: (1) file was created through VS Code, (2) file is actually Markdown format, (3) file has any content, (4) VS Code was used at all
SHELL COMMAND ISSUE: Command uses pipe '|' but doesn't set 'shell': true in config, which may cause the pipe to fail (get_vm_command_line defaults shell=False)
SEMANTIC MISMATCH: The evaluator cannot distinguish between a file created through VS Code vs any other method (terminal, file manager, etc.)
WEAK FILE CHECK: Only verifies string presence in ls output, could match directories or partial filename matches
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace 'is_extension_installed' with 'compare_answer' metric for proper string comparison
Add 'shell': true to the vm_command_line config to ensure pipe works correctly
Use more robust file existence check: 'test -f /home/user/Desktop/README.md && echo 'exists' || echo 'not found'
Consider checking file type with 'file' command to verify it's a text/markdown file

Note: Instruction requirement 'through VS Code' cannot be verified with file system checks alone - consider simplifying instruction to just 'Create and save README.md to Desktop' or add VS Code-specific verification if critical
